units.title: tasks.v1 contract: TasksService rpcs, messages and event payloads
units.notes: Package tasks.v1, no go_package. Task (title, notes, priority LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/URGENT, deadline as date + optional local time, status OPEN/DONE, assignee user ids), Birthday (name, day, month, optional year, remind_days_before). RPCs: List/Create/Update/Complete/Reopen/DeleteTask, List/Create/Update/DeleteBirthday, Get/SetFamilySettings (IANA timezone, default from device), ConnectGoogle (auth code + PKCE verifier + redirect uri), DisconnectGoogle, ListGoogleCalendars, SetGoogleCalendar, GetGoogleConnection, ListMyDueReminders / AckReminder / SnoozeReminder (1h | tomorrow 09:00) / GetDigest for the telegram scheduler. Event messages TaskAssignedEvent, TaskDueEvent, BirthdayUpcomingEvent. Brief defaults adopted for every open question.

units.title: Task handlers + Connect layer with family scoping and assignee restriction
units.notes: Tests: family A cannot read/change family B tasks; assignees must be members of caller's family. Titles/notes bounded in runes. Errors via rpc.Internal. Rules (coordinator, from reviews): Handlers fail closed on fmauth.FromContext error (the internal :9090 listener has no auth interceptor). UpdateTask: due_on "" clears date AND time; due_time without a date -> InvalidArgument; formats YYYY-MM-DD / HH:MM in the family timezone (schedule.ParseDeadline). due_at is always set when due_on is set (date-only = end of local day, schedule.Deadline.At). AssigneeList presence: absent = unchanged, present-empty = clear all, else replace. Assignees must be members: refresh via family.Client.ListMembers(caller bearer, family) over the PUBLIC listener and upsert known_members + DeleteKnownMembersExcept in one InTx (the query refuses an empty keep list). ReopenTask clears completed_by_user_id (CHECK enforces). ListTasks keeps SQL order (due_at NULLS LAST, urgent>high>medium>low); DONE filter sorts by completed_at desc in Go. Reminders are created at WRITE time: Create/Update -> per assignee UpsertReminder(kind task_due, occurrence = due_at RFC3339, remind_at = schedule.TaskRemindAt) + DeletePendingRemindersForItemExcept(keep assignees, occurrence); Complete/Delete -> DeletePendingRemindersForItem(task_due); Reopen -> re-create. Typed constants: task_reminders.kind 'task_due'|'birthday'; calendar_links.kind 'task'|'birthday'. Every authenticated RPC (shared caller helper) calls TouchKnownMember(caller family, caller user, claims email) so known_members is filled even for families that never assign a task. E8 (2026-10-06): recorded commit corrected from literal HEAD to 344d108; shortfalls are reworked in u12b.

units.title: Birthday handlers + Connect layer
units.notes: Family scoping tests for birthdays; age/next occurrence from u10. Rules (coordinator, from reviews): Validate with schedule.ValidateBirthday (rejects 29 Feb with a non-leap year and future dates). Age shown only when year != 0 (Occurrence.HasAge), never infer from turning_age == 0. DeleteBirthday deletes pending task_reminders (kind birthday) for it. Create/UpdateBirthday also run the ListMembers refresh of known_members (upsert + DeleteKnownMembersExcept in one InTx). E8 decision 1: start from git stash 'autopilot 0003/u13: birthday handlers'.

units.title: Reminder scheduler loop publishing tasks.task.due and tasks.birthday.upcoming
units.notes: Injected clock; dedupe via reminder_deliveries (channel=push). Rules (coordinator, from reviews): Before publishing any reminder, check the recipient with family.Client.IsMember(family, user) over the INTERNAL client; if false skip it and DeleteKnownMember (known_members can be stale). Birthdays: recipients = known_members of the family (each IsMember-checked); materialise yearly occurrences with schedule.NextOccurrence + BirthdayRemindAt(now) (past times dropped). Dedupe per channel via reminder_deliveries (RecordDelivery 'push'); scan with ListDueReminders(now, 'push'). Birthday recipients come from known_members (filled by u12's TouchKnownMember and the u12/u13 ListMembers refresh). On IsMember ERROR (family down): skip this tick for that recipient — no RecordDelivery, no DeleteKnownMember.

units.title: Reminder and digest RPCs for the telegram scheduler (ListMyDueReminders, Ack, Snooze, GetDigest)
units.notes: Per-user, called with the linked user's token. Dedupe channel=telegram. Digest: today's tasks, overdue, upcoming birthdays. Rules (coordinator, from reviews): SnoozeReminder rewrites remind_at (sets snoozed_until, clears acked_at) AND ClearDeliveries for that reminder in the same InTx, so it fires again; works on already-acked reminders. Snooze option via schedule.SnoozeUntil (rejects unknown). reminder_id is the task_reminders uuid (fits a 64-byte Telegram callback with a short prefix). AckReminder records channel 'telegram' delivery. ListMyDueReminders uses ListDueRemindersForUser(channel 'telegram') and IsMember-checks nothing (caller is the user). GetDigest: date = schedule.Today(family tz); due = schedule.DigestDue(now, tz, last sent); MarkDigestSent per user.

units.title: Google connect / disconnect / list + pick calendar RPCs; FailedPrecondition when OAuth unset
units.notes: Per-member connection. With client id/secret empty: service starts, ConnectGoogle returns FailedPrecondition with a clear message (tested). Rules (coordinator, from reviews): SetGoogleCalendar stores the real calendarList id (never "primary") and deletes the user's old calendar_links when the calendar changes. DisconnectGoogle calls gcal.Revoke then deletes the connection and links. ConnectGoogle maps gcal.ErrInsufficientScope / ErrMissingRefresh to FailedPrecondition with a clear message; ErrClientConfig -> Internal (log, no Google body). Never overwrite the stored email from Refresh output (it returns none). Seal the refresh token with crypto.Box.Seal(token, crypto.Owner(family, user)); never store raw Google error bodies in last_error or logs. E9 decision 1: SetGoogleCalendar calls calsync.Pusher.SwitchCalendar before storing the new calendar; it never deletes calendar_links directly. E4 decision (option 1, 2026-10-06): ConnectGoogle accepts a serverAuthCode from Google Sign-In on Android and exchanges it with the Web client id/secret and an EMPTY redirect URI (no PKCE verifier).

units.title: Calendar push sync: task/birthday -> Google event create/update/delete
units.notes: Completed task keeps its event with a check-mark title prefix (brief default). Birthdays as yearly all-day events. Tests use gcal fake. Rules (coordinator, from reviews): We OWN the events (gcal.UpdateEvent is a PUT): user additions such as location are not preserved — accepted. Never resurrect: if the linked event was cancelled in Google and the pull has not run, run pull for that connection first or skip. Events need a duration: date-only = all-day (end date exclusive, next day); timed = 30 minutes ending at the deadline. Skip pushing into a calendar the family already has a link in (CalendarLinkedInFamily) so shared calendars do not get duplicates. Keep calendar_links until the Google delete succeeds; sweep ListOrphanCalendarLinks. gcal.ErrForbidden = lost writer access: set last_error, ask the user to pick another calendar (not reconnect). E9 decisions (2026-10-06): (1) The calendar switch is owned by calsync: add Pusher.SwitchCalendar(ctx, family, user) that, under each item's lock, deletes the user's events in the OLD calendar treating ErrForbidden and ErrNotFound as gone (log calendar_id+event_id of abandoned events) and drops those links; u20's SetGoogleCalendar calls it instead of deleting links itself. pushTo then treats a link whose calendar differs from the connection's as stale: drop the link without touching Google, then insert. (2) Inserts use gcal.EventID(...) (u18b): ErrConflict on insert means our event already exists -> UpdateEvent that id and save the link, so retries/timeouts/concurrent pushes never duplicate. Keep the per-item lock, taken BEFORE reading the item in PushTask/PushBirthday; SweepOrphans locks per link; evict idle item mutexes. Single tasks replica is assumed (recorded in u24 notes). (3) ListOrphanCalendarLinks also returns task links whose task has due_on IS NULL (sqlc regenerate). Start from git stash 'autopilot 0003/u21: calsync push'.

units.title: Hook calendar push into task and birthday handlers

units.title: Calendar pull sync: incremental syncToken polling applies Google edits/deletes
units.notes: No watch channels (non-goal). Event edited in Google updates title/deadline; deleted event deletes task/birthday. Rules (coordinator, from reviews): Pull semantics: a cancelled event (Google returns only id+status) deletes the linked task/birthday — map through GetCalendarLinkByEvent, never through extendedProperties. Edits pull title/notes/date back. Clamp/skip titles (1-200 trimmed) and notes (<= 4000) from Google so the sync token always advances; 410 -> full resync.

Rules (coordinator, from reviews): Wire TASKS_FAMILY_ADDR (family :9090, internal RPCs) AND TASKS_FAMILY_PUBLIC_ADDR (family :8080, token-forwarded ListMembers) — both required at startup. bus.EnsureStream(ctx, "tasks") before the publisher and scheduler; /healthz -> database.HealthHandler(pool, 0); subscribe family.member.removed -> DeleteKnownMember. The family.member.removed subscriber (internal/members/removed.go + test) deletes the known_members row, the user's pending task_reminders and their task_assignees rows in that family. E9: run exactly one tasks replica (calsync per-item lock is in-process); compose/prod must not scale tasks.
